D008_l001.question:
A 42-year-old married male police officer presents with episodic mood and energy disturbances. Over a 2-week period, he experienced a distinctly elevated and euphoric mood accompanied by markedly increased energy and psychomotor activity. During this interval, he demonstrated pronounced overconfidence and grandiose self-assessment uncharacteristic of his baseline, markedly reduced need for sleep without associated fatigue, and increased distractibility with attention drawn to minor environmental stimuli. He exhibited notable social over-engagement, initiating excessive interactions and activities, resulting in clear occupational and interpersonal impairment.

This was followed by a 1-month period characterized by a pervasive sense of emotional blunting, with difficulty experiencing normal affective responses. He reported persistent fatigue despite adequate opportunity for rest, along with sleep fragmentation characterized by frequent nocturnal awakenings and difficulty returning to sleep. Cognitive symptoms included marked indecisiveness affecting routine daily choices and persistent, intrusive self-reproach focused on past minor errors. During this depressive phase, he engaged in a suicide attempt, involving preparatory and potentially lethal self-harm behavior, leading to significant functional decline in both occupational performance and family roles.
D008_l001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D008_l002.question:
A 48-year-old married male factory supervisor presents with episodic mood disturbance characterized by distinct manic and depressive phases, each associated with significant functional impairment at work and home.

Over a period of approximately 2 weeks, he experienced a markedly elevated and irritable mood with pronounced psychomotor agitation, reporting an inability to remain still or relax. During this time, he engaged in excessive work-related activity, initiating multiple new projects beyond his usual responsibilities. He described markedly reduced need for sleep without associated fatigue, and displayed inflated self-importance with beliefs of having a special role and mission. His attention was easily captured by minor external stimuli, leading to distractibility and disorganized task completion. Occupational functioning was substantially compromised, with conflicts at work and impaired judgment.

This was followed by a depressive phase lasting approximately 1 month, characterized by pervasive low mood, frequent crying episodes, hypersomnia, and persistent fatigue despite extended sleep. He reported feelings of worthlessness, reduced self-confidence, and subjective cognitive difficulties, particularly forgetfulness attributed to poor concentration. He endorsed recurrent passive thoughts of death without a specific plan. During this period, he had marked difficulty fulfilling occupational duties and family responsibilities.
D008_l002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder
